entities.name: An-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qaitbay
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
An-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qaitbay was the son of Qaitbay, and a Mamluk sultan of Egypt from 7 August 1496 to 31 October 1498, when he was assassinated.

    Born around 1450 in Cairo, Egypt, An-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qaitbay was the ruler of Egypt during a pivotal moment in world history. His reign marked the beginning of the end of the Mamluk Sultanate, a powerful Islamic empire that had dominated North Africa and the Middle East for nearly three centuries.

    An-Nasir Muhammad's tenure was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Ottoman Empire, which had been expanding its territory in the region. He also oversaw significant architectural and cultural developments in Egypt, including the construction of several new mosques and madrasas.

    Despite his efforts to resist the Ottoman threat, An-Nasir Muhammad's reign was cut short when he was assassinated on 31 October 1498. His death marked the end of the Mamluk Sultanate and paved the way for the Ottoman Empire to conquer Egypt and establish a new era of Islamic rule in the region.

    An-Nasir Muhammad's legacy continues to be felt in Egypt and beyond, with his military campaigns and architectural projects serving as a testament to the enduring power of the Mamluk Empire.
